headline: High: shared MCP/network surfaces create default-path prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error risks between Haystack and OpenMetadata.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes REST APIs and MCP servers with broad network egress, while OpenMetadata also exposes MCP server and event/webhook surfaces. That creates a plausible default-path instruction bridge if OpenMetadata ingests Haystack outputs or vice versa. The pairwise interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata consumes Haystack-generated text from MCP, APIs, or webhooks without provenance filtering, injection is possible.
IF Haystack forwards untrusted content into MCP or REST tool calls, that content can steer OpenMetadata actions.
mitigations: Disable automatic execution of instructions found in retrieved content.
Add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages.
Restrict MCP tools to allowlisted operations only.
Insert a human review step before any action-taking tool call.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents onto separate workspaces or brokers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call REST/MCP endpoints; OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, memory, and tribal-knowledge data classes and exposes APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. Even without explicit shared storage, the pair can move sensitive operational metadata across a third-party boundary. The evidence is docs-only, so I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF either agent is configured to ingest the other's outputs into prompts or logs, sensitive metadata can leak across the pair.
IF OpenMetadata events or webhooks carry governed metadata to Haystack over egress, that data leaves its original control boundary.
mitigations: Minimize fields sent between agents.
Redact identifiers and lineage details before transfer.
Turn off unnecessary webhooks and event subscriptions.
Use separate credentials and principals for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace or tenant isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and mutable APIs/SDKs/events/webhooks, while Haystack can call REST APIs and MCP servers with broad egress. Their overlapping write-capable surfaces can conflict on shared mutable resources if orchestrated together. No locking or coordination primitive is documented here, so uncertainty again favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same catalog, queue, or downstream API without external locking, updates can race.
IF Haystack triggers OpenMetadata mutations through MCP while OpenMetadata processes concurrent events, state conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Serialize writes through one orchestrator.
Use idempotency keys on all mutations.
Add optimistic concurrency checks.
Pause event ingestion during bulk updates.
requires-engineering: implement resource-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG system that can generate retrieved facts, and OpenMetadata is a data-collaboration/governance layer that can consume and propagate metadata through APIs, events, and webhooks. If OpenMetadata treats Haystack output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream catalog or governance actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata uses Haystack output as a source of truth without verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF Haystack-generated metadata is auto-published into OpenMetadata events or webhooks, downstream consumers may act on errors.
mitigations: Require source citations before publishing facts.
Add validation rules for imported metadata.
Route high-impact changes to manual approval.
Compare Haystack output against authoritative sources.
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and rejection thresholds.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, memory, and tribal knowledge data classes, while Haystack handles anonymous usage statistics and broad egress. The profiles do not state residency or certification boundaries, but the governance-oriented data classes make compliance mismatch plausible if data is routed through Haystack. Because the relevant controls are undocumented, I keep this at medium.
conditions: IF governed metadata from OpenMetadata is sent to Haystack for processing, retention or residency rules may be violated.
IF the deployment requires strict deletion/export handling for lineage or governance data, cross-agent routing can break compliance.
mitigations: Classify data before any transfer.
Block regulated fields from leaving OpenMetadata.
Document retention and deletion paths.
Review vendor DPAs and residency settings.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement at the integration boundary.
